# Load packages

```{r packages, echo=FALSE}
# install.packages(c("easystats", "readr", "knitr", "ggplot2"))
library(easystats)   # loads datawizard, see, correlation, report, etc.
library(readr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r read-data, echo=FALSE}
dat <- read.csv("The_Significant_Five_dataset.csv") 
```

# Table: proportion of Yes / No

Replace `q_yesno` with your Yes/No column name.

```{r yes-no-table}
vars <- c("embarrassed_easily", "self_conscious", "pay5_lateness", "buy20_shirt")

labels <- c(
  embarrassed_easily = "Gets embarrassed easily in minor awkward situations",
  self_conscious     = "Feeling self-conscious when making a small mistake in front of others",
  pay5_lateness      = "Paying $5 to silently check-in due to lateness",
  buy20_shirt        = "Paying $20 to change a new shirt due to a large stain on the old one"
)

make_row <- function(v) {
  x <- dat[[v]]
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]

  n_yes <- sum(x == 1)
  n_no  <- sum(x == 0)
  total <- n_yes + n_no

  data.frame(
    Question = labels[[v]],          # <- uses the friendly label
    Yes   = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_yes, 100 * n_yes / total),
    No    = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_no,  100 * n_no  / total),
    Total = total
  )
}

yes_no_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, make_row))

knitr::kable(
  yes_no_table,
  row.names = FALSE,
  align = c("l", "c", "c", "c"),
  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "Number and percentage of Yes and No answers"
)
```

# Scatter plot: two Likert-scale questions

Likert items are discrete (e.g., 1-5), so points overlap heavily. Using
`geom_jitter()` spreads them out so you can see density. Replace `likert_a`
and `likert_b` with your column names.

```{r likert-scatter}
ggplot(dat, aes(x = general_embarrassment, y = judgment_worry)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#0072B2") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "general_embarrassment", y = "judgment_worry",
       title = "Relationship between General embarrassment and Judgement worry") +
  theme_modern()    # theme from the 'see' package (easystats)

ggplot(dat, aes(x = judgment_worry, y = communication_discomfort)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#0072B2") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "judgment_worry", y = "communication_discomfort",
       title = "Relationship between Judgment worry and Communication discomfort") +
  theme_modern()

ggplot(dat, aes(x = communication_discomfort, y = general_embarrassment)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#0072B2") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "Communication Discomfort Level", # please fix this, just don't use underscores for plotting
       y = "general_embarrassment",
       title = "Relationship between Communication discomfort and General embarrassment") +
  theme_modern()
```
